body:
## Pull request overview

Aligns ObjectUI’s dashboard widget typing/validation with the `@objectstack/spec` shorthand widget format and improves React reconciliation by generating non-`undefined` widget keys.

**Changes:**
- Updated `DashboardWidgetSchema` (TypeScript + Zod) to support both legacy `{ component }` widgets and spec shorthand `{ type, options }`.
- Updated dashboard renderers to use typed `widget.type/widget.options` and added an index-based key fallback.
- Added renderer tests for shorthand metric widgets and (intended) key uniqueness coverage.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts | Makes widget Zod fields optional and adds `type/options` for spec shorthand. |
| packages/types/src/complex.ts | Makes widget interface fields optional and adds `type/options` for spec shorthand. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx | Removes `as any` for `type/options`, adds index-based key fallback, updates widget mapping. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardGridLayout.tsx | Removes `as any` for `type/options`, aligns shorthand mapping for chart/table. |
| packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/DashboardRenderer.widgetData.test.tsx | Adds tests for shorthand metric rendering and intended key uniqueness verification. |
</details>

This test claims to verify unique React keys, but it never asserts that React emitted no key warnings (e.g., via a `console.error`/`console.warn` spy). Consider adding an explicit assertion that the "Each child in a list should have a unique \"key\" prop" warning is not logged, otherwise this test can pass even if keys are still duplicated.

DashboardWidgetSchema is now fully optional (id/component/type/options), so an empty widget object would pass validation. Consider modeling this as a union (legacy: requires component; shorthand: requires type) or add a Zod refinement to require at least one of `component` or `type` so invalid widgets are caught early.

The updated DashboardWidgetSchema interface makes both `component` and `type` optional, which allows invalid widget shapes at compile time and forces downstream consumers to handle impossible states. Consider expressing this as a discriminated/union type (legacy component format vs spec shorthand) so TypeScript enforces that at least one rendering strategy is present.

`widgetKey` can still be non-unique when multiple widgets share the same `title` and have no `id` (keys will collide on `title`). To guarantee unique sibling keys, consider incorporating `index` into the title fallback (or another deterministic unique suffix) whenever `id` is missing.
